metadataReview.note: The National Army Museum names Peitsang (Beicang) as the place of a Chinese defeat on the allied march from Tianjin to Beijing, alongside Yangtsun on 5-6 August 1900. The locator is the gazetteer point for Beicang, whose alternate names include the older romanisation Pei-ts'ang, used as a sector reference; the fetched sources do not map the Chinese entrenchments or the allied lines of attack. The existing date of 5 August 1900 is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames 1816781 (Beicang, Tianjin, feature code P.PPLA4; alternate names Beicang Zhen, Pei-ts'ang, 北仓, 北仓镇) publishes latitude 39.2357 and longitude 117.12262, rounded to [117.1226,39.2357]. Nominatim returns the 北仓镇 (Beicang town) boundary relation 18798650 about 0.6 km away at 39.2361921, 117.1158422. The National Army Museum equates Peitsang with Beicang. This is the seat point of the present town, used as a sector reference for the 1900 engagement; it is not a surveyed entrenchment, a troop position or the centre of the fighting. No accuracy radius is claimed.
